investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable with the message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. The pod therefore never starts, the eval runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling logic in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent call), and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create — requiring vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — is entirely unmet.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 147s before the eval timed out.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150898, status=fail — the check ran for ~151s, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency breach.

sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with latencyMs=151260, confirming the capacity exhaustion affects every pod creation attempt for the remote-agents feature.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with latencyMs=151452, a third independent confirmation that no kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call is the earliest point that would trigger pod scheduling, and the scheduler rejection prevents any subsequent evidence from being written.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler message, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any single additional pod will fail.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883): if cleanup failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing available capacity for new probe pods.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster may have been sized with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for concurrent eval probes plus live workloads, causing contention during peak scheduling windows.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable with the message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. The pod therefore never starts, the eval runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling logic in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent call), and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create — requiring vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — is entirely unmet.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 147s before the eval timed out.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150898, status=fail — the check ran for ~151s, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency breach.

sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with latencyMs=151260, confirming the capacity exhaustion affects every pod creation attempt for the remote-agents feature.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') with latencyMs=151452, a third independent confirmation that no kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call is the earliest point that would trigger pod scheduling, and the scheduler rejection prevents any subsequent evidence from being written.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler message, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any single additional pod will fail.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883): if cleanup failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing available capacity for new probe pods.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster may have been sized with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for concurrent eval probes plus live workloads, causing contention during peak scheduling windows.
